text:
Sam K: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector rollout we saw host CPU p95 spike on ingress parsing for short-seq requests. p99 latency up ~120ms for small chat requests. Flame: https://dash.internal/trace/8135792461. Root looks like tokenization + gRPC small-write churn.
Elaine M: Yup, dashboards show p95 CPU 3.2 -> 6.1 on the hostgroup. Top symbols from perf: tokenize_buffer(), grpc_writev_small(), parse_frame().
Ravi P: My hunch — selector fell back to the large-batch kernel for tiny batches. That kernel does an extra memcpy path and allocs when seq_len < 64 but batch_hint==large. Could explain tokenization/alloc noise.
Jen L: I also noticed KV cache eviction rate doubled in the same window — kv_hits dropped ~18%. Might be batching reshuffle changing key locality.
Sam K: Good point. If batching reorders requests, kvcache shard hotness can change. Can we tag requests with stable shard hints while we test kernels?
Marco G: @infra-bot kicked off a perf run on a small canary (10% traffic) with kernel-hint toggled. Trace id: 0xDEADBEEF.
infra-bot: deploy started: canary kernel-hint=prefer-small for hostpool-ingress-1. Status: in-progress :rocket:
Elaine M: Local canary perf samples: tokenize_buffer (18%), grpc_writev_small (21%), kv_get (9%), kernel_large_memcpy (14%). The kernel memcpy shows up as a flat hotspot.
Ravi P: Actionable: force kernel selection to prefer small-batch kernel when seq_len<64 && batch_size<8. Also reduce the memcpy path by switching to in-place tokenize for small payloads.
Jen L: I'll prototype an in-place tokenize that reuses the per-request slab. Quick snippet: ```c
// reuse slab allocation
char *buf = slab_alloc(req->sz);
int out = tokenize_into(buf, req->sz);
// avoid temp string copies
```
Sam K: Plan: 1) canary kernel-hint change 2) implement slab reuse in tokenizer 3) coalesce small writev calls (<=4 writes) to cut grpc_writev_small churn. If p99 improves, roll forward. Owners: Ravi -> kernel-hint; Jen -> tokenizer slab reuse; Elaine -> telemetry/metrics.
Marco G: I'll wire the rollout with rollback triggers: error_rate>0.5% OR p99_regression>50ms -> auto rollback.
Jen L: Creating PR for slab-reuse + unit tests. Will run perf harness after merge. ETA ~2h.
Elaine M: Canary finished: p99 down ~90ms vs baseline, kv_hits back to previous baseline, host CPU p95 reduced by ~1.8. Preliminary diagnosis: kernel selector + small allocs amplified gRPC small-write overhead and caused kv thrash.
Sam K: Great. Next steps: merge slab-reuse & kernel-hint, add a regression test in ingress-perf-suite that emulates many short-seq (<64) chats, and add telemetry to assert kvcache hit rate doesn't drop >5% after kernel changes.
Ravi P: I'll open the kernel-hint PR and include a fallback test to ensure we don't pick large kernel for tiny batches.
Marco G: After merge I'll schedule a staged rollout and keep the auto-rollback window for 24h. Ping me if anyone sees anomalies. :thumbsup:
Jen L: PR up, running perf jobs now.
Elaine M: I'll draft a short postmortem and add the perf diffs to the runbook.
Sam K: Thanks team — good catch. We'll follow up with the postmortem and add the regression harness.
